title: IPO Report Card: 30 to 60 Days After Listing — November 2026
description: Many companies that listed 30 to 60 days ago are currently trading above their initial public offering (IPO) price. Several companies are also trading below t.

faq.a: An IPO (Initial Public Offering) is when a private company first offers its shares to the public to raise money, allowing ordinary people to buy a part of the company.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mainboard and SME IPOs?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger, more established companies that list on the main exchanges (NSE or BSE). SME IPOs are for Small and Medium Enterprises, which list on separate platforms (NSE Emerge or BSE SME) with different rules, often involving smaller issue sizes and different trading dynamics.

faq.q: How do I calculate my return?
faq.a: To calculate your return, you subtract the IPO price from the current price, divide by the IPO price, and then multiply by 100 to get a percentage. For example, if you bought at ₹100 and it's now ₹120, your return is ((120-100)/100) * 100 = 20%.
The "issue price" is the fixed price per share at which a company offers its shares to the public during an IPO.
The "current price" is the latest trading price of a share on the stock exchange at the time of reporting. It reflects what buyers and sellers are agreeing upon right now.
